tagline: Up Beaver Canyon into the old volcanoes of the Tushars.
intro: In Beaver, 200 North turns into Highway 153 and heads east for the mountains. A mile past the old racetrack the houses give out, and Beaver Creek runs alongside into a pretty canyon, the road narrow near its mouth. Inside the national forest the byway twists and climbs 4,000 feet through mountain mahogany and ponderosa pine, passing four hydroelectric plants on the way up.
The Tushars ahead look like a plateau and are not one. They are what is left of a series of old volcanoes, rich in minerals, and Delano Peak, the highest of them, stands above 12,000 feet.
season: Visit Utah calls it an especially fine drive for autumn color.

moments.title: Beaver
moments.text: The birthplace of Butch Cassidy, and the first town in Utah to be electrified, from a hydroelectric plant built on the Beaver River early in the 20th century.

moments.title: Merchant Valley Dam
moments.text: Above the steep forested climb the dam holds the water that runs the power plants below, and behind it the road levels off across flat alpine meadowland.

moments.title: Eagle Point
moments.text: Past the ski area's low-key cluster of homes the road reaches 9,200 feet, which makes it Utah's fifth-highest paved road, and the asphalt ends at Puffer Lake.

practical: Snow tires or chains are required in Beaver Canyon from November 1 through March 31. Beyond the end of pavement at Puffer Lake, Highway 153 is a dirt road that is closed in winter.

sources.label: Visit Utah, Central Utah Backway: Beaver Canyon and the Sevier River Valley
